title: Glasgow surname and research-study newspaper records
scope: Pre-1800 priority continuation: 51 full-name forms previously queried in both Irish collections, plus 16 abbreviation queries; worldwide spelling checks and extra original highlights remain bounded and incomplete. Nine earliest unresolved shipping passages are now excluded. A direct 1768 Philip Glasco marriage report is retained. The separate 1800–1850 log records 59 distinct queries, 758 retrieved entries, 735 readable first previews and 45 newly resolved original pages; later work remains incomplete.
conclusion: Verified Glasgow/Glasco/Glascow surname passages are retained with original links, approved excerpts and record-specific identity assessments. Repeated readings share one card while every issue is preserved. The 1786 Omagh marriage and 1793 business contact probably concern one James Glasco; no existing-profile identity or family attachment is proved. Wider pre 1800 searches remain incomplete.
limitations: Inspected catalogue pages and retained surname pages are different counts. The place-study notice is not surname evidence.
The 1829 page is the original of a previously known derivative extract, not a second independent occurrence.
The newspaper marriage date is 22 February 1802; the maintained OPR citation gives 23 February. The 1835 appeal heading varies between reports.
Large keyword searches remain incomplete; OCR can join unrelated columns or miss a surname. No new founding-family connection or live WikiTree edit is claimed.
Licensed scans and reading captures remain private; stable original image links are published.

The 1871 Belfast death notices repeat one notice and are not independent confirmations of age. One attempted source download returned HTTP 429; that passage remains unread. Nearby surname hits without an established connection were not added to the local family account.

Certain documentary father–son relationship; identification of Robert with Glasgow-2656 or Glasgow-3941 remains qualified. Counsel’s reference to Robert’s sons supports a qualified brother inference for co-plaintiff William. The uncle’s paternal or maternal side and all mothers are unstated. No parents are established for John Glasgow-2058.
Cookstown notices lacking age or relatives are not automatically assigned to the uncle or younger partner.
Belfast News-Letter gives the Ohio elder’s age as 55; attributed Belfast Mercury gives 56. The 1875 Parsonstown notice is outside the pre-1870 window.
The supplied 1821 meeting signature and 1828 jury occurrence are James Glasgow, not William; the coffee agent is only B. Glasgow. Blank/duplicate crops do not add events.
Ireland-country results are separately indexed from Northern Ireland. The wider 134-entry result set and alternative OCR spellings have not been exhausted.

The 4 October worldwide and 1600–1749 coverage totals are raw search metadata with only the stated first page/first ten surveyed. Exact-name retrieval was complete for the listed queries, but passage inspection was partial for William, Andrew and Thomas; both outstanding Andrew IDs are now resolved as vessel/city passages. Nine newly catalogued Margaret pages remain pending original passage review; additional Margaret and Elizabeth matches on two existing pages remain uninspected. Same-name queries are not exhaustive surname coverage because OCR variants, women’s notices and non-English forms may be missed.

The revised pre-1800 pass screens first previews, not every match on every page. All sixteen Dublin watchmaker originals are now read and saved; they repeat one advertisement. Both Irish geographic collections and six older spellings were checked separately; quoted names alone miss line divisions and OCR variants. No completeness claim for pre-1800 people or pre-1900 newspapers is made.

All 51 catalogue name forms were searched in both Irish collections, but abbreviations, further spellings and additional page highlights remain. The worldwide quoted John Glasco query returned zero despite a verified 1799 occurrence found with broader Glasco, demonstrating an exact-name OCR miss. Neither London record supports a family amendment.

1800–1850 coverage is first-preview triage of 48 quoted-name queries plus one contextual query, not all 83 forms or every match. No new profile relationship is marked certain or saved live. Name, occupation and locality support qualified comparison, not automatic profile attachment.

James NI153 entries were fully retrieved;151 first previews read,two whole-page crime duplicates too small. Every page carousel was not exhausted. New nine originals are privately captured; current profile call/ordination correction is locally queued, not saved live.

John NI 95 and Ireland 109 first previews were all screened; their repeated merchant advertisements are not independent family confirmations. A separate damaged 1849 marriage reading stays pending. Co-signatories are not necessarily relatives; Castledawson 4 July is the opposing meeting, not their residence/signing date. Probate-office locality and grant year do not prove residence or date of death.

Parallel continuation on 4 October 2026: worldwide Glascow loaded 180 of 306 results before a provider result-loader failure; the later Glafco search showed 21 previews, all loaded, but not all originals were inspected. Search counts changed between observations. Abbreviation zero results do not establish absence. Pre-1800 completeness has not been established across all digitised newspapers or all highlights.

The expanded long-s variant search displayed 28 matches but 27 unique preview cards were retrieved. Newly inspected 1746 and 1765 originals are retained; other previews remain leads. Complete pre-1800 coverage has not been established.

5 October 2026 batch: 9 additionalpre 1800 surname pages with excerpts. WorldwideGlascow loading gaps and external-worker capture failures remain unresolved; query cards and OCR/no-match results are not verified absences. Date boundaries in profile indexes are not actual event years.

By 5 October 2026, all 27 unique retrieved worldwide Glafco original pages were examined: 12 confirmed surname pages, 12 non-surname contexts and three ambiguous single-name/alias notices. The displayed total of 28 versus 27 cards remains unexplained. Glascow narrower queries retrieved further metadata but not every original. Confirmed surname pages and saved excerpts are integrated; no exhaustive pre-1800 claim is made.

5 October 2026 third batch: thirty additional original surname pages and two contextual headings saved. All nineteen Glafcoe cards and thirteen Samuel Glafgow cards were checked on originals; reprints remain separately cited but repeated readings share cards. Broader Glascow retrieval and additional highlights still prevent an exhaustive pre-1800 claim.

rows.reading: Hugh Allan v. Trustees of Robert Glasgow: the report calls Mrs Robertson Glasgow the late Robert’s natural daughter and first heir under his 1818 entail. It reports his death in 1827 and a supplementary entail and trust dated 23 June 1821, involving Seafield near Ayr.
rows.assessment: Contemporary account of the 25 August hearing, independently supporting Anne’s daughter/heir description and the 1827 death year. It does not verify 19 April. Hugh Allan-8034, the profile-defined nephew, is a compatible appellant candidate; older Allan-8028 has no death recorded but would be 109. Neither identity is proved. These later deeds are distinct from the uninspected 1803 trust.

rows.reading: House of Lords appeals: the report reproduces clauses of Glasgow’s settlement and says Lord Brougham recommended reversing the judgment below; judgment reversed accordingly. The heading appears to read Henry Allen v. Trustees of R. Glasgow.
rows.assessment: Reports the Wednesday judgment, 2 September 1835. The estate, Seafield dispute and counsel identify the same litigation as the 26 August report, whose appellant is Hugh Allan. Preserve the discrepant heading; compare the original court papers before resolving the name. Reported deed extracts are not an inspection of the original deed.

rows.reading: Shocking catastrophe at Rasharkin: Robt. Glasgow, described as a neighbour at Lisnagaver, warned James M’Caughern about a dangerous gable before it fell; Glasgow narrowly escaped while leaving the doorway and raised the alarm.
rows.assessment: Genuine Glasgow surname in a local incident. Robert-938 and Robert-3449 remain compatible candidates; no age, parents, occupation or link to a valuation holding is stated. A later Scottish death does not exclude Robert-938 being in Ireland in 1861.
